title: Bibimbap
kicker: A rice bowl of individually seasoned vegetables, a fried egg, and gochujang — then you wreck it all with a spoon.
story: Bibimbap means 'mixed rice', and the mixing is the point — but the magic happens before it: each vegetable is cooked separately and seasoned on its own terms. Spinach dressed with sesame and garlic. Bean sprouts with a whisper of chili. Carrots sweet and soft, mushrooms savory and browned. Nine little side dishes that become one giant one.

The bowl rewards two upgrades. First, a crackling rice bottom — either a hot stone bowl (dolsot) or a well-oiled skillet that toasts the rice against the pan while everything sits. Second, gochujang sauce loosened with sesame oil and a touch of sugar, painted across the top. Then the instruction the dish was named for: mix like you mean it, until every grain of rice has an opinion.
fun_fact: Jeonju, the food capital credited with bibimbap's origin, holds an annual Bibimbap Festival. The royal court version reportedly used up to a dozen seasoned vegetables.

steps.title: Season each vegetable alone
steps.text: Blanch spinach, squeeze hard, dress with sesame oil, garlic, salt. Simmer sprouts, dress with sesame oil and a pinch of chili. Sauté carrots until sweet-soft, zucchini until just wilted, mushrooms until browned with a splash of soy. Everything gets its own moment — this is what separates bibimbap from a stir-fry pile.

steps.title: Cook the beef (or double the mushrooms)
steps.text: Quick marinade of soy, sugar, sesame oil, garlic, 15 minutes. Sear hot until caramelized at the edges, 3-4 minutes.

steps.title: The gochujang sauce
steps.text: Stir gochujang with sugar, rice vinegar, sesame oil and a teaspoon of water until it flows lazily off the spoon. Taste — warm, sweet, gently ferocious.

steps.title: Build the bowl
steps.text: Hot rice in a warmed bowl, vegetables arranged in wedges around the center like a color wheel, beef in one wedge, fried egg on top. Sesame seeds. Paint sauce across the egg.

steps.title: Mix. Finally.
steps.text: The whole show exists so you can destroy it in ten seconds. Fold everything through the rice — sauce reaches every grain. For the crackling bottom, let the bowl sit on high heat two more minutes before mixing and listen for the sizzle.

notes: The seasoned vegetables keep 3 days refrigerated — bibimbap is a magnificent weekday assembly job.
No dolsot? A screaming-hot cast-iron skillet under the rice bowl for 3 minutes fakes the crackle convincingly.
Namul (the seasoned vegetables) double as Korean side dishes on their own.

storage: Namul refrigerate 3 days; gochujang sauce a month. Rice and eggs fresh each time. Assembled bowls should be eaten immediately — mixed bibimbap waits for no one.

facts.first_recorded: Late 1800s — first written down in the cookbook Siuijeonseo
facts.name_means: Literally 'mixed rice' (bibim = mixed, bap = rice). The recipe is the instruction manual for itself.
facts.technique: Every component cooked separately, mixed only at the table
facts.signature: Toasted sesame, gochujang warmth, crackling stone-bowl rice
facts.serve_at: Hot, with a raw egg yolk you stir in yourself
facts.pour: Makgeolli, or barley tea if it is lunch

relations.cluster_note: Bowls over rice where everything is cooked separately, then mixed at the table — by you, with intent.
